action: Update N-central to 2026.4.1 HF3 or later and the Patch Management Component to 2.14.4.5829 or later. Read the two N-able bulletins linked from the advisory and the N-able release notes. If an IT provider runs N-central for you, ask for confirmation.
exec: A second Canadian advisory in a week on a tool that IT providers use to reach client systems; ask your provider to confirm it is patched.
plain: Canada's cyber agency told organisations that use N-able N-central, a tool IT providers use to manage customers' computers, to install the newest fix. Two weaknesses are named, including one that lets someone skip the login.

key_findings: Affected: N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 and the N-central Patch Management Component before 2.14.4.5829.
CVE-2026-129271 is a local privilege escalation in N-central Patch Management.
CVE-2026-129272 is an authentication bypass on the MMS3 appliance through a predictable passcode.
The advisory makes no statement on whether either flaw is being exploited.
recommendations: Review the N-able advisories for CVE-2026-129271 and CVE-2026-129272 linked from the advisory.
Apply the necessary updates as they become available.
Check the N-able status page release notes for the fixed builds.

sources.name: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security alerts and advisories feed

summary: Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1165 tells Canadian organisations that N-able N-central before 2026.4.1 HF3 and its Patch Management Component before 2.14.4.5829 need updating. It names two flaws: a local privilege escalation in Patch Management and an appliance authentication bypass through a predictable passcode. The advisory does not say whether either is being exploited. It follows an earlier N-able advisory, AV26-1143, on November 12.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issues N-able N-central advisory AV26-1165

validation.note: CVE-2026-129272 was not found in NVD at the last check.
